newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OCC issues suggestions for stored-value cards.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OCC issues suggestions for stored-value cards.

text.p: Recognizing a fast-growing area in financial transactions, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on Tuesday issued suggestions to banks for handling smart cards and stored-value cards.

"Stored-value cards can take a lot of different forms," Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig said in a statement. "As banks consider whether and how they may become involved in this technology, it is critical for them to understand the risks, as well as the opportunities."
Stored-value cards typically have magnetic strips or computer chips charged with a fixed amount of value that can be spent in a similar way to coins or bills.
Smart cards -- plastic cards with computer chips embedded in them -- may function as stored-value cards and may also contain limited information and perform some computing functions.
In a bulletin for the banks, the OCC described some of the risks involved in handling the cards, such as card malfunctioning, loss of cards and the use of counterfeit cash.

Pointing out that banks can serve a variety of roles such as issuers of the cards and redeemers of the electronic cash, the agency advised banks to make clear which party will bear responsibilty at each stage of an electronic transaction.

"Thus far, transactional rules for some electronic cash systems are not well estabilished by current law," the OCC said. "Accordingly, in many important respects, the transactional rules for such systems must be established by contract."

The OCC also advised banks to make consumers aware of their rights and responsibilities when using stored-value cards. It pointed out that the cards outwardly resemble debit and credit cards but may expose customers to different risks.

In addition to the guidelines from the OCC, another bank regulatory agency, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp, said that on Thursday it will sponsor a public hearing on stored-value cards and similar electronic payment systems.
